title: Count frequencies
description: Write a function `count_frequencies(items)` that returns a dictionary mapping each distinct element of the list `items` to the number of times it appears in that list.
hints: You need to accumulate a running count for each distinct item as you go through the list.
A dictionary can act as a counter: `dict.get(key, default)` returns a fallback value when the key is not yet present.
Start with an empty dict and loop over `items`, updating it with `counts[item] = counts.get(item, 0) + 1` for each item, then return `counts`.
expected_behavior: Returns a dict where each key is a distinct element from `items` and each value is how many times that element occurs in `items`.
explanation: `counts.get(item, 0)` reads the current count for `item`, defaulting to 0 the first time it is seen, so each iteration safely increments the running total without a KeyError, building up a full frequency table by the time the loop ends.
